title: Chest CT-Derived Body Composition and Systemic Inflammation for Predicting One-Year Mortality in Hospitalised Acute Exacerbations of COPD: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Purpose Acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) carry substantial one-year mortality. Systemic inflammatory indices and computed tomography (CT)-derived body-composition measures each hold prognostic value but have not been combined. We examined whether integrating them improves prediction of one-year all-cause mortality in hospitalised AECOPD patients and quantified the incremental value of the radiological axis. Patients and methods In this single-centre retrospective cohort, 380 consecutive AECOPD patients admitted to a secondary-level hospital in Türkiye (May 2024-November 2025) were included; 336 with complete one-year follow-up formed the primary cohort. Inflammatory indices (C-reactive protein [CRP], albumin, LDH-to-albumin ratio [LAR], and others) and CT parameters (pectoralis muscle area [PMA], vertebral attenuation, pulmonary artery-to-aorta ratio) were evaluated. Predictors were selected by LASSO regression with stepwise refinement; nested logistic models were compared by the DeLong test on a single common analytic sample, and a nomogram was internally validated with 1000 bootstrap resamples. Results Eighty-two patients (24.4%) died within one year. Cross-domain correlations between inflammatory indices and radiological parameters were uniformly weak (|r| < 0.21). In the common analytic sample (n = 272), a parsimonious model (age, male sex, ICU admission, albumin, CRP, LAR, PMA) reached an AUC of 0.849 (95% CI 0.793-0.904), exceeding the radiological (0.810) and clinical (0.740) models; the increment of the full combined model over the inflammatory model was modest (ΔAUC +0.029; p = 0.029). In the model's own complete-case cohort (n = 318) the apparent AUC was 0.864 (optimism-corrected C-index 0.846; Hosmer-Lemeshow p = 0.539). Nomogram tertiles stratified observed one-year survival from 98% to 42% (log-rank p < 0.001). Conclusion Adding CT-derived body composition to a routine clinical-inflammatory panel produced a small but measurable gain in discrimination. Pending external validation, the tool may aid admission risk stratification, most usefully in patients whose serum albumin is already perturbed.

title: Diagnostic and Therapeutic Challenges of Mycobacterium avium Complex Pulmonary Disease in Patients with Lung Cancer: A Retrospective Case Series.
abstract: Objective To describe the clinical characteristics, diagnostic challenges, and therapeutic management of Mycobacterium avium complex pulmonary disease (MAC-PD) in patients with lung cancer, and to highlight the diagnostic limitations and treatment dilemmas encountered in this vulnerable population. Methods We retrospectively reviewed four patients with lung cancer complicated by MAC-PD at a tertiary respiratory center in Beijing, China, between 2017 and 2025. Clinical data, cancer characteristics, underlying structural lung disease, anticancer treatments, radiological findings, microbiological results, anti-MAC regimens, and clinical outcomes were analyzed. Diagnostic methods included sputum culture, bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) next-generation sequencing (NGS), and T-SPOT.TB. The 2020 ATS/ERS/ESCMID/IDSA diagnostic framework for NTM-PD was referenced for case evaluation. Results All four patients were male, aged 66-73 years (mean 70.5 years), with underlying bronchiectasis or structural lung abnormalities. Two had lung adenocarcinoma and two had squamous cell carcinoma. MAC-PD was detected during early anticancer therapy (n=1), during combined chemotherapy and immunotherapy (n=1), or after lung cancer surgery (n=2). Chest CT showed centrilobular nodules, tree-in-bud opacities, bronchiectasis, cavitary lesions, destroyed lung, and bronchopleural fistula, overlapping with tumor progression or bacterial pneumonia. MAC was identified by BALF NGS in three patients and sputum culture in one. In Cases 1, 2, and 4, clinical diagnoses of suspected MAC-PD were supported by BALF NGS without confirmatory mycobacterial culture. Causative organisms included M. intracellulare (n=2) and Mycobacterium avium complex not further speciated (n=2). All patients received multidrug anti-MAC therapy. Regimens were modified in two patients due to adverse events or drug-drug interactions. Two patients with destroyed lung and bronchopleural fistula had poor outcomes despite prolonged therapy (30 months and 17 months, respectively). No patient underwent antimicrobial susceptibility testing. Conclusion MAC-PD should be considered in lung cancer patients with bronchiectasis or structural lung disease when new centrilobular nodules, tree-in-bud opacities, cavitary lesions, or progressive lung destruction cannot be explained by tumor progression. Early bronchoscopy with both culture and NGS is essential; NGS should be regarded as an adjunct to, not a substitute for, culture-based diagnosis and susceptibility testing. Drug-drug interactions-particularly rifamycin-antifungal combinations-require proactive evaluation, and the combination of rifapentine with voriconazole should be avoided. Once destroyed lung develops, treatment options are limited and prognosis is poor, underscoring the importance of early detection.

title: Admission Vascular Pedicle Width and in-Hospital Mortality in Intensive Care Unit Patients with Acute Pulmonary Edema: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the association between admission vascular pedicle width (VPW) and in-hospital mortality in critically ill patients with acute pulmonary edema, together with interobserver reliability and mortality discrimination. Patients and methods This retrospective cohort included 223 adults admitted to intensive care with clinically and radiographically confirmed acute pulmonary edema of presumed hydrostatic origin. Two blinded observers measured VPW on the first anteroposterior chest radiograph obtained within one hour of presentation, and their arithmetic mean was analyzed. Reliability was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients and Bland-Altman analysis. Multivariable logistic regression assessed adjusted associations; receiver operating characteristic analysis assessed discrimination. Clinical models with and without VPW underwent bootstrap internal validation. Results In-hospital mortality was 28.7% (64/223). Median VPW was greater in nonsurvivors than survivors [84.9 (75.7-93.4) vs 67.4 (59.2-77.1) mm; p<0.001]. Reliability of the mean of the two observers' measurements was good [ICC(2,2)=0.897; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.866-0.921], although proportional bias was present (p<0.001). After adjustment for Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II (APACHE II) score, Charlson Comorbidity Index without its age component, sex, chronic kidney disease, and ejection fraction, each 10-mm increase in VPW was associated with higher odds of mortality (adjusted odds ratio=2.458; 95% CI, 1.775-3.403; p<0.001). VPW alone yielded an AUC of 0.790 (95% CI, 0.725-0.855). In exploratory analyses, adding VPW increased the optimism-corrected clinical-model AUC from 0.791 to 0.872. Conclusion Greater admission VPW was independently associated with in-hospital mortality. VPW may provide complementary prognostic information from routinely acquired chest radiographs, but prospective external validation is required.

title: An Update on Blood-Brain Barrier Penetrating Nanoparticles for the Treatment of Glioblastoma.
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is an aggressive and lethal primary brain malignancy, with patient survival largely unchanged over recent decades despite advances in surgery, radiotherapy and chemotherapy. A major therapeutic challenge is the blood-brain barrier (BBB), which restricts the delivery of many systemically administered drugs, including emerging biologic and gene-based therapies. Nanoparticle (NP) delivery systems have therefore attracted intense interest to overcome BBB-associated transport limitations, enhance tumor specificity and enable delivery of potent therapeutic cargos to infiltrative GBM cells. This review provides an overview of some recent advances in BBB-penetrating NP platforms for GBM treatment, spanning lipid-based, polymeric, dendrimer, inorganic, peptide-based and biomimetic systems. We discuss several extracellular and intracellular biological barriers to effective delivery, while outlining how these challenges may inform rational NP design. Targeting strategies exploiting a range of receptors are reviewed alongside stimuli-responsive systems and combination approaches that integrate BBB modulation techniques, including focused ultrasound and intranasal nose-to-brain delivery. While many NP platforms demonstrate compelling preclinical efficacy, translation to the clinic remains limited. We therefore discuss recent clinical developments and highlight select translational opportunities such as preclinical model selection, manufacturing scalability factors and regulatory considerations. As such there may be a need for integrated design strategies, clinically relevant model systems and robust biodistribution and toxicity assessment. Aligning advances in nanotechnology with GBM biology and clinical constraints may be essential in realizing the therapeutic promise of BBB-penetrating nanomedicines to improve outcomes for patients with this devastating disease. Collectively, BBB-penetrating NPs may represent a promising strategy for GBM treatment, and bridging the gap between preclinical success and clinical benefit may remain an opportunity for the field.

title: Open Salvage Microwave Ablation for Refractory Diffuse Hepatic Oozing After Abandonment of Planned Hepatectomy for Large Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: We report a 50-year-old man with hepatitis B-related compensated Child-Pugh A cirrhosis, an 8.9-cm primary hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and a suspected 1.7-cm satellite nodule, who was initially planned for hepatectomy. During hepatic mobilisation, persistent diffuse surface parenchymal oozing developed. Despite conventional topical haemostatic measures and a 12-minute Pringle manoeuvre, severe oozing (estimated blood loss approximately 2000 mL) was only partially controlled. Given the pre-existing portal hypertension, continued resection carried a high risk of post-hepatectomy liver failure, and hepatectomy was therefore abandoned. Rather than simple haemostasis and abdominal closure without tumour-directed therapy, open intraoperative ultrasound-guided microwave ablation (open IOUS-MWA) was performed to achieve dual objectives: local oncological control and consolidation of haemostasis. Importantly, this scenario is distinct from previously reported MWA for discrete tumour-related bleeding, in which ablation is used primarily for haemostasis. Three-month follow-up contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (CE-MRI) identified residual disease despite post-operatively initiated concurrent targeted-immunotherapy, necessitating supplementary percutaneous MWA. No extrahepatic metastasis was detected during follow-up; however, durable local tumour control could not be confirmed, and the oncological benefit cannot be attributed exclusively to this salvage ablation. Larger cohorts with prolonged follow-up are needed to validate this approach.

title: Self-Attention-Based Deep-Learning Model Using Multimodal MRI to Predict Ki-67 Expression and Recurrence-Free Survival in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: Purpose To assess multimodal gadolinium-enhanced MRI-based deep learning fusion schemes for preoperative Ki-67 expression estimation in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and clarify their correlation with recurrence-free survival (RFS). Patients and methods This retrospective study enrolled 297 patients with pathologically confirmed HCC. All patients underwent preoperative 3.0-T multimodal gadolinium-enhanced MRI, including T1- and T2-weighted, arterial, portal venous, delayed and hepatobiliary phases. Single-sequence models were developed using a 3D ResNet-50 network. Three fusion models were developed: Deep Learning Image Fusion model (DL-IF), Decision Fusion model (DL- DF ), and Self-Attention Feature Fusion model (DL-SAFF). Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses identified independent clinical predictors, which were subsequently used to build the Deep Learning-Clinical Self-Attention Feature Fusion model (DLC-SAFF). Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) and Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analyses were applied to visualize model spatial attention and quantify feature contributions. Prognostic value was assessed using follow-up data. Results Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) were identified as independent indicators linked to elevated Ki-67 expression in HCC. DL-SAFF reached a validation area under the curve (AUC) of 0.816, surpassing results from DL-IF (AUC: 0.735) and DL- DF (AUC: 0.792). The DLC-SAFF model further improved performance (AUC: 0.828, 95% CI: 0.74-0.92). Decision curve analysis indicated higher net benefit for DLC-SAFF across thresholds of 0.11-0.71. SHAP analysis demonstrated that hepatobiliary phase and delayed phase features were the dominant contributors to model prediction. The DLC-SAFF model identified high Ki-67 patients with a shorter median RFS (18.59 vs 47.73 months, p = 0.0011). Conclusion The DLC-SAFF model enables noninvasive prediction of Ki-67 expression in HCC using multimodal MRI and shows potential for risk stratification, offering a promising tool to guide preoperative biological assessment and individualized treatment planning.

title: Visceral and Ectopic Fat Remodeling with Incretin-Based Therapies in Type 2 Diabetes: Human Imaging Evidence.
abstract: Incretin-based therapies change the distribution of adipose tissue and ectopic lipid during weight loss. This narrative review examines human imaging evidence across abdominal, hepatic, pancreatic, cardiac and skeletal-muscle fat during treatment with selective glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists and dual- and triple-receptor agonists. Adults with type 2 diabetes are the primary population; findings from mixed diabetes populations and obesity-related disorders are identified separately. The central question is how depot responses relate to overall weight loss and organ outcomes. Hepatic fat has the most mature evidence, and visceral-fat reduction is supported across multiple studies. Tirzepatide provides the most extensive linked multi-depot imaging dataset, while recent survodutide findings extend GLP-1/glucagon imaging evidence to abdominal fat in obesity without diabetes. Cardiac and skeletal-muscle studies extend assessment to tissue composition and ventricular remodeling; pancreatic, renal sinus and other perivascular responses remain exploratory. Imaging modality, anatomical coverage, segmentation and endpoint definition vary across studies, and receptor comparisons are uneven in their populations, comparators and depots assessed. Remodeling is predominantly weight-associated, with selected studies identifying disproportionate hepatic or visceral responses. Imaging can connect these responses to the organ phenotype of interest: hepatic disease activity, cardiac structure or muscle composition. The next step is to test whether repeated depot measurements improve prediction of functional and clinical outcomes beyond routine weight and metabolic assessment.

title: Epidural Steroid Injection Approaches Across the Spine: A Practical Narrative Review of Technique, Indications, and Contrast Patterns.
abstract: Background Epidural steroid injection (ESI) is among the most frequently performed image-guided interventions for spinal pain. The strongest evidence supports its use for radicular pain, particularly lumbar radicular pain from disc herniation, while evidence for nonspecific axial or discogenic pain is weaker and approach-dependent. The route used to reach the epidural space (caudal, interlaminar, or transforaminal) has major implications for drug distribution, effectiveness, and safety. Objective and scope This narrative review offers a practical overview of considerations for performing ESI in the cervical, thoracic, lumbar, and sacral regions, integrating the authors' clinical experience with current medical society guidance. We describe the relevant anatomy, techniques, indications, and limitations of the various approaches. Techniques and approaches Particular attention is given to the transforaminal approach, contrasting the subpedicular ("safe triangle") technique with the infraneural (Kambin/retrodiscal) technique, a distinction that applies primarily to thoracolumbar injection; to the contralateral oblique (CLO) view for interlaminar depth assessment; and to caudal delivery under fluoroscopic and ultrasound guidance. Contrast patterns A core section addresses the systematic recognition of an epidurogram versus off-target patterns (intravascular, intrathecal, subdural, and fascial/retrodural flow), illustrated with fluoroscopic images, since pattern recognition is central to safety and effectiveness. Safety The review summarizes corticosteroid selection, dosing and frequency, radiation protection, and antithrombotic management, and stratifies complications by frequency, severity, and approach. Where terms such as "mandatory" or "only acceptable" are used, they reflect the published recommendations of the International Pain and Spine Intervention Society (IPSIS), the World Institute of Pain (WIP) Benelux work group, or allied multisociety consensus. Conclusion Image guidance, contrast confirmation, judicious steroid selection, and etiology-driven patient selection remain the foundations of safe and effective ESI. The recommendations synthesized here represent evidence-informed expert consensus rather than high-level comparative evidence for every point.

title: Ultrasound-Guided Thoracic Paravertebral Block with Liposomal Bupivacaine versus Conventional Ropivacaine for Thoracic Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Purpose This meta-analysis aimed to systematically compare the perioperative efficacy and safety of ultrasound-guided thoracic paravertebral block (TPVB) with liposomal bupivacaine (LB) versus conventional ropivacaine in adults undergoing video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS), with postoperative opioid consumption as the primary outcome. Patients and methods PubMed, the Cochrane Library, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from inception to July 8, 2026. Eligible studies comparing LB with ropivacaine for TPVB were screened, and pooled analyses were performed in Stata 16.0 using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models. Standardized mean differences (SMDs) were used for continuous outcomes and odds ratios (ORs) for binary outcomes. Certainty of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. Results Four randomized controlled trials (RCTs; 327 patients) were included. The primary outcome showed no statistically significant between-group difference in cumulative 24-hour postoperative opioid consumption (SMD = 0.30, 95% confidence interval (CI) -0.35 to 0.94; P = 0.368; I 2 = 87.9%; very-low-certainty evidence). Resting pain scores at 24 hours were lower in the LB group (SMD = 0.54, 95% CI 0.12 to 0.96; low-certainty evidence), although clinical importance could not be established from the pooled SMD alone. The ropivacaine group had higher odds of intraoperative vasoactive-agent use (OR = 3.15, 95% CI 1.60 to 6.22; two trials), and length of stay was modestly shorter in the LB group (SMD = 0.30, 95% CI 0.00 to 0.59); both findings were supported by low-certainty evidence. Other pooled secondary outcomes showed no statistically significant differences. Conclusion Current evidence does not establish a clinically meaningful or opioid-sparing advantage of LB over ropivacaine for TPVB after VATS; a non-significant difference does not demonstrate equivalence. Possible differences in 24-hour resting pain, intraoperative vasoactive-agent use, and length of stay remain uncertain and require confirmation in larger, methodologically rigorous randomized trials.

title: A Longitudinal Comparison of Baseline Predictors of Five-Year OAG Development.
abstract: Purpose To compare sensitivities for prediction of development of open angle glaucoma (OAG) in 5 years in eyes initially assessed as clinically suspect open angle glaucoma in a prospective longitudinal study. Methods Data were collected prospectively every fourth month for five years from both eyes of 88 subjects with at least one clinically glaucoma suspect eye. Presently, observations at occasions 1, 2, 15 and 16 were analyzed. An eye was considered clinically glaucoma suspect eye if it met at least one of the criteria: suspicious ophthalmoscopic optic nerve head appearance, ocular hypertension, pigment dispersion syndrome, exfoliation syndrome, or visual field asymmetry. Measurements of mean deviation (MD) with standardized automatic perimetry (SAP) were used for classification of OAG at 5 years follow-up. The OAG conversion criterion was defined as a mean SAP MD below the critical limit for normality (-3.7 dB) across occasions 15 and 16. At specificity of 95% for measurement at baseline, 95% confidence intervals for sensitivity were estimated for intraocular pressure (IOP), cup-to-disc ratio (C/D-vertical) and neuro-retinal rim area (NRA), both measured with confocal scanning laser ophthalmoscopy (CSLO) and nerve fiber layer thickness measured with laser scanning polarimetry (GDx TSNIT-global) and optical coherence tomography (OCT cpRNFLT-global), respectively. Confidence intervals were estimated using Hilgers, Delta-Wald with logit transformation, and Bootstrap strategies. Results During the 5-year follow-up, 20 clinically suspect eyes met the OAG conversion criterion. The different strategies resulted in confidence intervals of the same order. The 95% confidence intervals estimated with Bootstrap strategy were 0.57 [0.30;0.84] for OCT cpRNFLT, 0.32 [0.08;0.61] for GDx TSNIT, 0.30 [0.08;0.59] for HRT NRA, 0.26 [0.05;0.58] for HRT vertical C/D, and 0.11 [0.02;0.27] for IOP. Conclusions For the currently used MD-based OAG conversion definition, OCT-cpRNFLT has the highest sensitivity for prediction of OAG development at the initial visit among the morphometric variables. The low sensitivity for IOP questions the value of IOP slightly above 21 mmHg for prediction of OAG at baseline.

title: ERBB2 Exon 20 Mutation-Guided Trastuzumab Deruxtecan Therapy in Metastatic Lung Adenocarcinoma with Low HER2 Expression: A Case Report.
abstract: HER2 mutations are uncommon in lung adenocarcinoma, and treatment options become limited after failure of standard systemic therapies. We report a 69-year-old woman with metastatic lung adenocarcinoma involving multiple lymph nodes, bone, and the left adrenal gland. Histopathological and immunohistochemical examinations strongly supported a diagnosis of primary pulmonary adenocarcinoma. Targeted next-generation sequencing (NGS) performed at initial diagnosis in January 2024 identified an ERBB2 exon 20 in-frame insertion mutation (p.Y772_A775dup). The patient received six sequential treatment regimens, including platinum-based chemotherapy, PD-1 inhibitor therapy, antiangiogenic therapy, and palliative radiotherapy. Initial tumor regression was observed, but sustained disease control was not achieved. Following further disease progression, the previously identified ERBB2 mutation was reassessed by the multidisciplinary team in 2025. HER2 immunohistochemistry showed an IHC score of 1+. Based on the activating ERBB2 mutation, trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) was initiated in June 2025 at a fixed dose of 200 mg per administration (approximately 3.2 mg/kg), lower than the standard starting dose for HER2-mutant NSCLC. Five doses were administered between June and November 2025. Serum carcinoembryonic antigen and carbohydrate antigen 19-9 levels decreased markedly after treatment. Serial chest computed tomography indicated radiological disease stabilization for approximately 5 months, with no clinically significant treatment-related adverse events documented. This case highlights the value of molecular profiling in identifying actionable ERBB2 mutations despite low HER2 protein expression. It also provides a real-world observation of disease stabilization with a lower-than-standard initial dose of T-DXd, although conclusions regarding reduced-dose efficacy cannot be drawn from a single case.

title: Effect of Ultrasound-Guided versus Conventional Lung Recruitment on End-of-Surgery Atelectasis in Adults Aged 45-74 Years Undergoing Prone-Position Spinal Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to compare the effects of ultrasound-guided stepwise lung recruitment maneuver (LRM) versus conventional manual LRM on the incidence of end-of-surgery atelectasis in patients undergoing prone-position spinal surgery. Methods In this randomized controlled trial, 120 patients aged 45-74 years undergoing prone-position spine surgery under general anesthesia were randomized to ultrasound-guided group (n = 60) or conventional manual group (n = 60). Both groups received a fixed PEEP of 5 cmH 2 O intraoperatively. The primary outcome was the incidence of ultrasound-defined atelectasis at the end of surgery (T3). Results The final analysis included 60 patients in the intervention group and 59 in the control group. The incidence of atelectasis at the end of surgery (T3) did not differ significantly between groups [73.3% (44/60) vs 71.2% (42/59); RD = 2.1%, 95% CI: -13.9% to 18.2%; RR = 1.03, 95% CI: 0.82 to 1.29; P = 0.794]. Tidal volume at T3 was lower in the intervention group (385 ± 52 mL vs 437 ± 55 mL, P < 0.001), whereas dynamic compliance was comparable (37 ± 9 vs 36 ± 9 mL·cmH 2 O -1 , P = 0.517). No severe postoperative pulmonary complications occurred. Exploratory analyses suggested that higher T1 PaCO 2 was associated with an increased risk of newly emerged atelectasis at T3, whereas higher T1 heart rate and higher T2 PaO 2 were associated with a reduced risk of newly emerged atelectasis at T3. In the full cohort, T2 atelectasis was associated with T3 atelectasis, but the confidence interval was wide. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require external validation. Conclusion Under a fixed PEEP of 5 cmH 2 O, stepwise ultrasound-guided LRM did not demonstrate superiority over conventional manual LRM. Exploratory analyses suggested that T2 atelectasis and higher preoperative PaCO 2 may be associated with atelectasis at the end of surgery, requiring validation in an independent cohort. Trial registration Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2400086097; https://www.chictr.org.cn/). Registered on June 25, 2024.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Brain MRI Diagnosis: A Scoping Review and Evidence-Gap Map Across Neurological Diseases.
abstract: Introduction/objective Artificial Intelligence (AI), including machine learning and deep learning, is increasingly applied to brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) for disease detection, classification, segmentation, and clinically relevant prediction. This review aimed to map the evidence on AI-assisted brain MRI diagnosis, identify methodological and clinical translation gaps, and propose priorities for future research. Methods This scoping review was conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and Web of Science were searched for peer-reviewed English-language publications from January 2018 to April 2026. Data were charted according to disease domain, study design, AI method, dataset, validation strategy, performance metrics, explainability, and key limitations. Results The search identified 1,020 records. After duplicate removal and screening, 61 publications were included, comprising 24 original studies used for the primary evidence map and 37 reviews or commentaries used for contextual synthesis. Evidence was strongest for brain tumor imaging and Alzheimer's disease, whereas stroke, multiple sclerosis, pediatric neuroimaging, and rare neurological conditions were underrepresented. Most studies relied on public benchmark datasets and retrospective validation, whereas external validation, prospective clinical evaluation, subgroup analysis, explainability, and workflow integration were inconsistently reported. Discussion The findings indicate that AI-assisted brain MRI research remains unevenly developed and is constrained by dataset dependence, limited external validation, limited prospective clinical evaluation, and inconsistent reporting of explainability, subgroup performance, and workflow integration. Conclusion AI shows promising research-stage potential for brain MRI-based diagnosis, particularly in brain tumor analysis and Alzheimer's disease classification. Future research should prioritize multicenter validation, diverse and disease-specific datasets, explainable and equitable AI design, transparent reporting, and prospective evaluation within real clinical workflows.

This scoping review was conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews. Data were charted according to disease domain, study design, AI method, dataset, validation strategy, performance metrics, explainability, and key limitations.

Results

The search identified 1,020 records. After duplicate removal and screening, 61 publications were included, comprising 24 original studies used for the primary evidence map and 37 reviews or commentaries used for contextual synthesis. Evidence was strongest for brain tumor imaging and Alzheimer's disease, whereas stroke, multiple sclerosis, pediatric neuroimaging, and rare neurological conditions were underrepresented. Most studies relied on public benchmark datasets and retrospective validation, whereas external validation, prospective clinical evaluation, subgroup analysis, explainability, and workflow integration were inconsistently reported.

Discussion

The findings indicate that AI-assisted brain MRI research remains unevenly developed and is constrained by dataset dependence, limited external validation, limited prospective clinical evaluation, and inconsistent reporting of explainability, subgroup performance, and workflow integration.

Conclusion

AI shows promising research-stage potential for brain MRI-based diagnosis, particularly in brain tumor analysis and Alzheimer's disease classification. Future research should prioritize multicenter validation, diverse and disease-specific datasets, explainable and equitable AI design, transparent reporting, and prospective evaluation within real clinical workflows.

title: Primary Male Appendiceal Choriocarcinoma With Background of Low-Grade Appendiceal Mucinous Neoplasm: Diagnostic Challenges and Poor Prognosis.
abstract: Background/aim Choriocarcinoma is a highly aggressive trophoblastic malignancy that is most commonly gestational in origin. Non-gestational choriocarcinoma in the male gastrointestinal tract is extremely rare, and primary appendiceal involvement is exceptional. Case report We report such a case of a 75-year-old male who presented to the emergency room with severe abdominal pain. Physical examination indicated possible acute appendicitis suspicious for perforation, and computed tomography (CT) scans revealed a 7.5 cm mass in the lower right quadrant as well as numerous liver hypoechoic nodules. No lesions/nodules were identified in his testicles or mediastinum. Emergency surgery with right hemicolectomy and concurrent liver biopsy was performed. Pathology gross exam revealed a 7.5 cm appendiceal mass with associated appendiceal perforation. Histologically, the tumor showed a poorly differentiated carcinoma morphologically composed of syncytiotrophoblasts, cytotrophoblasts and intermediate trophoblasts with adjacent low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasm (LAMN). The carcinoma cells were positive for cytokeratin 7 (CK7), beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG), GATA-binding protein 3 (GATA 3) and Sal-like protein 4 (SALL4). These features supported a primary appendiceal choriocarcinoma and the liver biopsy demonstrated metastasis of choriocarcinoma with extensive tumor necrosis. Post-surgery lab tests also revealed an exceptionally high serum β-hCG titer of 289,308 mIU/ml. The patient underwent hospice care after surgery and expired one month later. Conclusion This is the first documented case of male primary choriocarcinoma with background of LAMN and poor prognosis. Recognition of the three carcinoma components in combination with the corresponding tumor immunohistochemical markers is the key for the precise diagnosis.

title: Implementation of a Prefecture-Wide Regional Referral System for Early Detection of Pancreatic Cancer in Hiroshima, Japan: Protocol for a Multicenter Prospective Observational Study (Hi-PEACE Project).
abstract: Background Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has a poor prognosis, and early detection is essential to improve clinical outcomes. However, many patients with early-stage PDAC are asymptomatic, complicating detection in routine clinical practice. Population-based screening for PDAC is not currently recommended given its low incidence and cost-effectiveness concerns. Therefore, regional collaboration between primary care physicians and specialist centers may facilitate identifying individuals with PDAC risk factors or suspicious pancreatic imaging findings warranting further evaluation. Objective This study aims to describe the protocol for a prefecture-wide regional collaboration program in Hiroshima Prefecture, Japan, and evaluate its operation and diagnostic yield, particularly for the detection of stage 0 or I PDAC. Methods The Hiroshima Pancreas Cancer Early Diagnosis With Collaboration and Examination (Hi-PEACE) project is a multicenter prospective observational study conducted in Hiroshima Prefecture. The project involves 20 core hospitals covering all 7 secondary medical care areas. Eligible participants are adults aged 20 years or older with PDAC risk factors or suspicious pancreatic imaging findings. Risk factor-based referral criteria include low- and high-grade risk factors based on relative risks in the Japanese Clinical Practice Guidelines for PDAC, previous studies on early-stage PDAC, and feasibility in primary care settings. Participants are identified through 2 pathways: risk factor assessment and imaging abnormalities, including indirect pancreatic findings such as main pancreatic duct dilatation, pancreatic duct stenosis, and pancreatic cysts. Individuals meeting referral criteria are referred to core hospitals for detailed pancreatic evaluation, with computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, endoscopic ultrasonography, and, when clinically indicated, pathological diagnosis. The primary outcome is the number and proportion of participants diagnosed with early-stage PDAC, defined as stage 0 or I disease, among participants referred through the Hi-PEACE project. Secondary outcomes include the number and proportion of participants diagnosed with PDAC and those who undergo surgical resection, distribution of PDAC risk factors and suspicious pancreatic imaging findings, diagnostic procedures performed at core hospitals, treatment status, and prognosis. The operation of the regional referral system will also be evaluated descriptively using annual referral volumes and the distribution of referrals across participating hospitals and secondary medical care areas. Results Participant enrollment began on November 20, 2022. As of December 31, 2025, a total of 9,866 participants had been enrolled, and enrollment is planned to continue until December 31, 2028. Data collection and analysis are ongoing. The overall study period is planned to last until December 31, 2030. Conclusions The Hi-PEACE project is a prefecture-wide collaborative program designed to promote early detection of PDAC through structured referrals to specialist centers. This study will provide information on referral activity and diagnostic yield, particularly for stage 0 and I PDAC, and may inform the development of similar regional early detection programs. Further comparative studies and long-term follow-up will be needed to evaluate the impact of such programs on clinical outcomes.

title: Orthodontic Management of Vertically Impacted Mandibular Permanent Second Molar in Adults: Case Report.
abstract: Impacted mandibular permanent second molars (MM2) are uncommon, with a reported prevalence of 1.8% to 3% among orthodontic populations, and vertically impacted MM2 are particularly infrequently reported. This case describes the orthodontic preservation of a vertically impacted tooth 47 in a 20-year-old Chinese male who presented with recurrent right-sided mandibular pain, gingival swelling, and bleeding associated with pericoronitis around tooth 48. Clinical examination revealed an Angle Class I molar relationship on the left and a Class II relationship on the right, a rightward mandibular midline deviation, 3 mm of anterior mandibular crowding, overeruption of teeth 17 and 27, and an unerupted tooth 47. Panoramic imaging showed vertically impacted teeth 18, 28, and 47, a horizontally impacted tooth 48, and mesioangular impaction of tooth 38. Cone beam computed tomography demonstrated the relationship between tooth 47 and adjacent structures and minimal resorption of the distal root of tooth 46, without obvious root dilaceration or clear ankylosis-related changes. Cephalometric findings included a skeletal Class I relationship, bimaxillary protrusion, proclined incisors, and a hypodivergent facial pattern. Following a discussion of extraction and implant replacement versus orthodontic retrieval, the patient selected preservation for psychosocial and economic reasons, with extraction planned if no movement occurred within 2 to 3 months. Treatment included fixed appliances, extraction of tooth 48, and surgical exposure of tooth 47. At month 6, with 0.017×0.025-inch stainless steel archwires in place, a customized 0.7-mm stainless steel loop with an approximately 10-mm distal extension was bonded to tooth 46. Elastic traction between this loop and the attachment on tooth 47 applied approximately 50 to 60 gf of extrusive force. Tooth 47 became visible at month 8, approximately half its crown was visible at month 11, and a buccal tube was then bonded for continued alignment. The tooth reached the occlusal level at month 13, and treatment was completed at month 14. Teeth 46 and 47 retained vital pulp responses, and no symptoms or apical pathologies were reported. Immediately after treatment, external root resorption of approximately 1 mm was observed on tooth 46; at 10 months, the corresponding radiolucent area was approximately 0.5 mm, with stable clinical findings and good oral hygiene. The outcome suggests that surgical exposure combined with tooth-borne orthodontic extrusion may be a feasible tooth-preserving option for carefully selected adults with vertically impacted mandibular second molars. Longer-term reports with standardized clinical and radiographic assessments are needed to define prognosis and broader applicability.

title: A Multiagent Large Language Model Framework for Longitudinal Multimodal Tracking of Wet Age-Related Macular Degeneration: Retrospective Feasibility Study.
abstract: Background Wet age-related macular degeneration (AMD) requires long-term, high-frequency management involving multimodal retinal imaging across repeated follow-up visits. Reconstructing disease trajectories from fragmented imaging reports, treatment histories, and clinical notes creates a substantial information integration burden for clinicians in routine chronic disease management. Objective This study aimed to evaluate the preliminary feasibility of a proof-of-concept, multiagent large language model (LLM) framework that integrates longitudinal multimodal imaging findings and treatment records into structured reports to support clinician review during wet AMD follow-up. Methods We developed a 3-layer multiagent LLM framework using GPT-4o and AutoGen. The framework consisted of modality-specific perception agents using a visual grounding prompting strategy, an integration agent, and a tracking report agent. To test technical feasibility, the framework was evaluated on a dense retrospective pilot dataset of 12 patients encompassing 69 long-term follow-up visits. AI-generated outputs were assessed against expert review at the visit level and through report-level quality scoring. Results In this exploratory cohort, the framework achieved a mean visit-level activity classification accuracy of 80.8% (SD 3.4%) across 4 independent runs (range 78.3%-85.5%), with a mean Cohen κ of 0.605 (SD 0.072; range 0.549-0.705). The framework generated structured longitudinal summaries of disease activity, multimodal findings, and treatment histories. The visual grounding prompting strategy reduced the nonimage reference rate from 13.8% (12/87) to 1.1% (1/87), supporting more consistent grounding of image-based outputs in visual evidence. Conclusions This proof-of-concept study supports the preliminary feasibility of using a multiagent LLM framework to organize longitudinal multimodal wet AMD follow-up data and produce structured summaries for clinician review. These reports are intended to support review of disease progression and treatment response associations during longitudinal follow-up. Future prospective multicenter studies with larger patient cohorts should evaluate whether these reports improve clinical workflow efficiency, reduce clinician workload, and support follow-up management decisions.

title: Performance of a Large Language Model for Predicting Clinical and Radiographic Outcomes in Knee Osteoarthritis: Single-Center Prospective Observational Study.
abstract: Background Large language models (LLMs) can extract information from unstructured clinical text, but it remains unclear whether their ability to assess current status translates into reliable predictions of longitudinal outcomes. Objective This study aimed to evaluate DeepSeek's ability to assess baseline clinical and radiographic status in knee osteoarthritis (KOA), its performance in predicting 6-month outcomes, and its interrun reproducibility. Methods This study used a single-center, prospective observational cohort design to conduct a blinded, retrospective evaluation of the LLM. A total of 128 patients with primary KOA were enrolled, of whom 111 (86.7%) completed the 6-month follow-up and were included in the primary analysis. DeepSeek-V4-Flash and a rheumatologist independently assessed KOA diagnoses, baseline Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC) scores, and Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) grading based on the same standardized interview records and imaging reports and predicted 6-month outcomes. The LLM was run independently 3 times. The actual outcomes determined by another senior physician served as the reference, and the results were compared with the physician's predictions and the persistence model. Results The LLM showed high baseline diagnostic agreement with the physician (105/111, 94.6%) and good agreement on the WOMAC and KL, but 6-month predictions (WOMAC mean absolute error=5.92-6.58; KL exact agreement=74/111, 66.7%-76/111, 68.5%) were worse than those of the physician comparator (mean absolute error=3.86; 96/111, 86.5%) and not superior to those of the persistence model (mean absolute error=5.43). Despite high interrun intraclass correlation coefficients (0.982 and 0.965), exact agreement between runs was poor (35/111, 31.5% and 7/111, 6.3%). Conclusions The evaluated DeepSeek configuration may support structured baseline KOA assessment. However, its 6-month predictive accuracy and patient-level stability remain limited. Prognostic applications require evidence of added value over a persistence model.

title: A Competency Assessment Tool for Liver Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound Among Sonography Trainees: Development and Multicenter Validation Study.
abstract: Background Despite the increasing use of liver contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS), no standardized, organ-specific tool exists for assessing trainees' cognitive competency. Existing instruments lack multidimensional evaluation and external validation, which limit training quality and patient safety. Objective This study aims to develop and validate the CEUS Competency Assessment for the Liver (CCAL), a tool to standardize the evaluation of theoretical and cognitive skills in liver CEUS. title: Comparison of Rule-Based Natural Language Processing and Diagnosis Code Approaches to Detecting Bleeding in the Electronic Health Record: Algorithm Validation Within a Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Background Anticoagulant use is prevalent and increasing. High-quality anticoagulation management balances individual thrombotic and bleeding risks to optimize care. An automated algorithm to accurately extract major bleeding events from the electronic health record (EHR) of a large health care system would be extremely useful for tracking outcomes of anticoagulated patients. Objective The study aims to assess the accuracy of a natural language processing (NLP) approach, compared with and in conjunction with a diagnosis code (Dx Code)-based strategy, for detecting major bleeding from the EHR. Methods Patients with at least 1 prescription for apixaban, dabigatran, edoxaban, rivaroxaban, or warfarin between January 1, 2019, and December 31, 2023, were analyzed for major bleeding events. Major bleeding was defined similarly to the International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis definition. For the NLP algorithm, clinical notes and radiology reports were screened for mentions of bleeding. MedTagger, an open-source, rule-based NLP tool, was then used on the notes. The NLP results were transformed into a feature set, which was used to create a support vector machine model. Three NLP models were created for central nervous system bleeding, critical site bleeding, and bleeding with a hemoglobin drop or transfusions (other major bleeding). Training and test datasets were created using an active learning approach. The model was trained using 80% of the dataset, while the remaining 20% was used for testing. After model finalization, an independent random sample was used to validate the model. Dx Codes were also used to detect major bleeding, similar to previously published approaches. Five unique algorithms were compared: (1) NLP, (2) Dx Code in the primary position, (3) Dx Code in any position, (4) NLP∩Dx Code in any position, and (5) NLP∪Dx Code in any position. All 5 algorithms were compared with manual chart review. Results The final analysis identified 111,338 patients prescribed outpatient anticoagulation during the study. Manual adjudication was performed for 1189 of the 111,338 (1%) patients. Most of the 5 approaches performed well on the test data, with F 1 -scores ranging from 0.545 to 0.959, except for Dx Code-Primary, with an F 1 -score of 0.353 for critical site bleeding. The F 1 -scores for the validation data ranged from 0.509 to 0.679. The NLP∩Dx Code in any position approach yielded excellent precision of 0.864 (95% CI 0.667-0.953) but only 0.559 (95% CI 0.395-0.711) sensitivity. The NLP∪Dx Code in any position approach yielded good sensitivity of 0.824 (95% CI 0.665-0.917) but only 0.368 (95% CI 0.269-0.481) precision. Conclusions Electronic tools can screen the EHRs to identify major bleeding outcomes in large patient cohorts within a multisite health care network with high precision but only moderate sensitivity. Additional work is needed to enhance sensitivity while maintaining high precision.

title: Topical Esomeprazole for the Prevention and Treatment of Radiation Dermatitis in Patients With Head and Neck Cancer: Protocol for a Phase 2 Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Background Radiation dermatitis (RD) is a common and clinically significant toxicity affecting the majority of patients undergoing external beam radiation therapy, particularly those treated for head and neck cancer (HNC). RD can impair quality of life, limit treatment intensity, and compromise oncologic outcomes; yet, there is no established standard-of-care for its prevention or management. Preclinical studies suggest that a topically reformulated proton pump inhibitor (PPI), esomeprazole (Dermaprazole), has antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antifibrotic properties that may mitigate radiation-induced skin injury. Objective This phase 2 randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the potential safety, feasibility, and efficacy of prophylactic topical Dermaprazole compared with standard supportive care (Aquaphor) in reducing the incidence and severity of clinically significant RD in patients with HNC receiving definitive chemoradiation. Methods This is a prospective, single-center, randomized controlled trial with a 2:1 allocation ratio. A total of 45 adults (≥18 y) with biopsy-confirmed head and neck malignancy planned to receive definitive chemoradiation of at least 66 Gy will be enrolled. Participants will be randomized to receive twice-daily topical Dermaprazole or Aquaphor beginning at computed tomography (CT) simulation and continuing through 2 weeks after completion of radiation therapy. The primary outcome is the rate and severity of RD, assessed weekly during treatment using the National Cancer Institute (NCI) Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) version 5 by the treating radiation oncologist, with blinded dermatologic assessment based on standardized medical photography. Feasibility outcomes include accrual rate, treatment compliance, and questionnaire completion rates. Secondary outcomes include time to onset and healing of grade ≥2 RD, quality of life assessed using the Skindex-16 instrument, radiation dose thresholds associated with dermatitis, and changes in inflammatory biomarkers (C-reactive protein, tumor necrosis factor-α, interleukin [IL]-1β, and IL-6). More specifically, secondary outcomes will be assessed through serial CTCAE version 5 evaluations for onset and healing, Skindex16 questionnaires for quality of life, radiation dose-volume parameters for dermatitis thresholds, and serum inflammatory marker concentration measurements before, during, and after treatment. Results The study began in June 2022 and has completed enrollment. Data analysis will commence following completion of data collection, with results expected to be published by 2027. Conclusions Should Dermaprazole demonstrate efficacy in reducing RD in patients undergoing radiation therapy, it may offer an alternative or adjunctive treatment option for the prevention and management of RD, potentially reducing treatment-related morbidity and improving patients' quality of life during radiotherapy. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04865731; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04865731. International registered report identifier (irrid) DERR1-10.2196/91035.

title: Integrating Multidimensional Clinical Data to Develop a Visual Nomogram for Individualized Prediction of Postinfectious Bone Loss in Patients With Spinal Infection: Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Postinfectious bone loss can lead to spinal instability and severe neurological complications, with potentially devastating outcomes. However, prognostic models to support individualized risk assessment remain limited. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a visual nomogram integrating multimodal clinical data to estimate postinfectious bone loss risk in patients with spinal infection and inform individualized monitoring strategies. This retrospective cohort study used consecutive sampling at Shandong Public Health Clinical Center. Baseline clinical and laboratory data were extracted from medical records. Eligible patients had confirmed spinal infection, a baseline vertebral bone destruction height ratio less than one-third, and complete baseline and follow-up data. Postinfectious bone loss was defined as a height ratio greater than or equal to one-third on computed tomography 12 months after baseline. Predictors were selected from 31 baseline variables using univariable logistic regression followed by least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Multivariable logistic regression was used to construct the nomogram. Internal validation used 500 bootstrap resamples, repeating all predictor selection and model-fitting steps. Performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, the Brier score, decision curve analysis, and clinical impact curve analysis. Postinfectious bone loss occurred in 48.9% (109/223, 95% CI 42.4%-55.4%) of patients. The nomogram combined infection characteristics (multidrug-resistant bacterial infection and infected spinal segment), skeletal status (osteoporosis), and laboratory markers (interleukin-6, albumin, and plasma fibrinogen) to estimate individual risk. In the multivariable model, the odds ratios (ORs) were 2.718 (95% CI 0.993-7.444; P=.05) for multidrug-resistant bacterial infection and 7.345 (95% CI 2.757-19.570; P<.001) for osteoporosis. Relative to cervical infection, ORs were 14.041 (95% CI 1.079-182.662; P=.04) for thoracic, 28.876 (95% CI 2.648-314.895; P=.006) for lumbar, and 12.604 (95% CI 0.436-364.075; P=.14) for thoracolumbar infection. Per unit increase, ORs were 1.004 (95% CI 0.996-1.012; P=.30) for interleukin-6 (pg/mL), 3.673 (95% CI 2.410-5.598; P<.001) for plasma fibrinogen (g/L), and 0.834 (95% CI 0.749-0.929; P=.001) for albumin (g/L). Discrimination remained high after optimism correction, with an AUC of 0.946 (95% CI 0.919-0.972), compared with an apparent AUC of 0.954 (95% CI 0.931-0.978). Calibration assessment yielded an intercept of 0.00 (95% CI -0.43 to 0.43) and a slope of 1.00 (95% CI 0.75-1.25), while the Brier score was 0.096 (95% CI 0.064-0.118), indicating close agreement between predicted and observed risks and low overall prediction error. This study developed a visual nomogram integrating baseline clinical characteristics, imaging features, and laboratory parameters to predict postinfectious bone loss in patients with spinal infection. Extending previous association studies to individualized risk prediction, the model showed good discrimination and calibration in internal validation. This approach may help identify high-risk patients and inform closer monitoring and timely reassessment before further structural deterioration and neurological complications.

title: The Digital Twin Paradigm in Head and Neck Cancer: Clinical Opportunities and Challenges.
abstract: Unlabelled Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) represents a significant public health challenge. Its treatment is characterized by high anatomical complexity and a critical need for functional preservation of speech, swallowing, and respiration. While multimodality care, including surgery, radiotherapy, and systemic therapy, has substantially improved patient survival, there are still high rates of life-altering toxicities and low response rates to immunotherapy. Current clinical decision-making largely relies on "digital snapshots"-static representations derived from population-based statistics and time point-specific imaging-which usually fail to account for the rapid anatomical and biological change during the course of treatment. Digital twins hold great promise in accelerating scientific breakthroughs and transforming oncology treatment and precision medicine through the creation of high-fidelity virtual patient representations that integrate real-time biological, anatomical, and clinical data. In this viewpoint, we propose 3 interconnected digital twins to establish a conceptual framework for the HNSCC digital twin. These digital twins include the anatomical twin, using virtual surgical planning and augmented reality for geometric precision; the dosimetric twin, using daily imaging and synthetic computed tomography generation for automated adaptive radiotherapy; and the biological twin, integrating deep phenotyping, radiomics, and mechanistic omics to simulate individualized therapeutic trajectories. Beyond acute care, we explore the clinical utility of digital twins in navigating the "de-escalation dilemma" for human papillomavirus-associated disease and improving survivorship through digital phenotyping. With the advent of longitudinal data from medical-grade Internet-of-Things sensors and circulating tumor DNA kinetics, digital twins can serve as active sentinels, detecting functional decline or subclinical events months before clinical manifestation. Furthermore, the implementation of synthetic control arms via virtual populations offers an avenue to accelerate clinical trials and address ethical issues in rare molecular subtypes. Despite this potential, substantial barriers to implementation remain, including profound anatomical instability during treatment, the "black box" nature of deep learning algorithms, and the challenges of multiscale data integration. We provide a technical roadmap for the development of "morphing" digital twins-dynamic systems capable of continuous geometric and biological auditing. By bridging the gap between the macroscopic world of radiation physics and the microscopic world of cellular evolution, digital twins may help shift the management of HNSCC from population-based statistical probability toward more individualized, biologically informed decision-making, with the goal of optimizing HNSCC management while preserving essential patient functions.

originalAbstract:

Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) represents a significant public health challenge. Its treatment is characterized by high anatomical complexity and a critical need for functional preservation of speech, swallowing, and respiration. While multimodality care, including surgery, radiotherapy, and systemic therapy, has substantially improved patient survival, there are still high rates of life-altering toxicities and low response rates to immunotherapy. Current clinical decision-making largely relies on "digital snapshots"-static representations derived from population-based statistics and time point-specific imaging-which usually fail to account for the rapid anatomical and biological change during the course of treatment. Digital twins hold great promise in accelerating scientific breakthroughs and transforming oncology treatment and precision medicine through the creation of high-fidelity virtual patient representations that integrate real-time biological, anatomical, and clinical data. In this viewpoint, we propose 3 interconnected digital twins to establish a conceptual framework for the HNSCC digital twin. These digital twins include the anatomical twin, using virtual surgical planning and augmented reality for geometric precision; the dosimetric twin, using daily imaging and synthetic computed tomography generation for automated adaptive radiotherapy; and the biological twin, integrating deep phenotyping, radiomics, and mechanistic omics to simulate individualized therapeutic trajectories. Beyond acute care, we explore the clinical utility of digital twins in navigating the "de-escalation dilemma" for human papillomavirus-associated disease and improving survivorship through digital phenotyping. With the advent of longitudinal data from medical-grade Internet-of-Things sensors and circulating tumor DNA kinetics, digital twins can serve as active sentinels, detecting functional decline or subclinical events months before clinical manifestation. Furthermore, the implementation of synthetic control arms via virtual populations offers an avenue to accelerate clinical trials and address ethical issues in rare molecular subtypes. Despite this potential, substantial barriers to implementation remain, including profound anatomical instability during treatment, the "black box" nature of deep learning algorithms, and the challenges of multiscale data integration. We provide a technical roadmap for the development of "morphing" digital twins-dynamic systems capable of continuous geometric and biological auditing. By bridging the gap between the macroscopic world of radiation physics and the microscopic world of cellular evolution, digital twins may help shift the management of HNSCC from population-based statistical probability toward more individualized, biologically informed decision-making, with the goal of optimizing HNSCC management while preserving essential patient functions.

title: Diagnostic Performance of Imaging-Based AI vs Radiologists for Preoperative Lymph Node Metastasis in Esophageal Cancer: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Imaging-based AI technologies, particularly deep learning and radiomics, offer a novel approach to improving the accuracy of lymph node metastasis (LNM) diagnosis. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of imaging-based AI models compared with radiologists in detecting preoperative LNM in esophageal cancer (EC). A systematic literature search was conducted across 5 databases (PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and IEEE Xplore) up to August 19, 2026. Eligible studies assessed imaging-based AI for preoperative LNM detection in EC (pathology reference standard). The protocol was prospectively registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO CRD420251169109). The PROBAST+AI (Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool with AI) tool was used for quality assessment. Bivariate random-effects models were used to calculate pooled sensitivity, specificity, diagnostic odds ratio (DOR), and area under the curve (AUC); between-study heterogeneity was described using τ² and I² (interpreted descriptively rather than categorically); homogeneity of study effects was tested with the Q statistic, and 95% prediction intervals (PIs) were derived for all pooled estimates. Head-to-head comparisons used a random-effects meta-analysis of within-study paired differences (restricted maximum likelihood with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman adjustment). A total of 18 studies were included. Across the 17 internal validation sets (2485 participants), AI models demonstrated a pooled sensitivity of 0.77 (95% CI 0.73-0.81; 95% PI 0.62-0.87), specificity of 0.79 (95% CI 0.73-0.84; 95% PI 0.48-0.94), a DOR of 12.88 (95% CI 9.57-17.33; 95% PI 4.5-37.0), and an AUC of 0.83 (95% CI 0.81-0.86; 95% PI 0.80-0.86). In the 10 head-to-head studies, AI showed higher sensitivity than radiologists (a paired difference of +0.27, 95% CI 0.11-0.37; 95% PI -0.26 to 0.45; P=.006) and higher discrimination (DOR ratio 4.65, 95% CI 2.53-8.56; 95% PI 0.97-22.42; P<.001), whereas specificity did not differ (+0.06, 95% CI -0.08 to 0.16; 95% PI -0.39 to 0.26; P=.30). Pooled arm-specific AUCs were 0.86 (95% CI 0.82-0.89; 95% PI 0.79-0.91) for AI and 0.67 (95% CI 0.59-0.75; 95% PI 0.44-0.84) for radiologists. In 4 external validation studies, pooled sensitivity was 0.66 (95% CI 0.46-0.81; 95% PI 0.31-0.90), specificity was 0.85 (95% CI 0.75-0.91; 95% PI 0.63-0.94), and the DOR was 10.42 (95% CI 3.50-31.01; 95% PI 0.6-142.0). These estimates remain subject to substantial heterogeneity and design-related bias. Imaging-based AI models demonstrated promising pooled diagnostic performance for preoperative LNM detection in EC. By pairing AI with radiologists' performance in the same cohorts, reporting PIs alongside CIs, and separating internal from external validation, this review provides a more realistic assessment than previous average-effect estimates. In predominantly retrospective and heterogeneous cohorts, AI had higher pooled sensitivity and discrimination than radiologists, whereas specificity did not differ; the selective extraction of the model with the highest AUC and very low certainty of evidence precludes conclusions about clinical superiority. These findings support AI as a decision-support tool, warranting prospective, multicenter external validation and prespecified human-AI comparisons rather than replacing radiologists.

title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging-Based Measurement of Pediatric Head Circumference by a Clinician-in-the-Loop 3D Surface Tool: Development and Validation Study.
abstract: Background Head circumference (HC) is a routine clinical parameter in pediatric patients indicating brain growth and neurodevelopment. Although usually obtained with a tape measure, this method is operator-dependent and prone to variability. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides a retrospective alternative, but existing imaging-based approaches can be limited by predefined measurement planes, restricted clinician review, and cranial surface artifacts. Objective This study aimed to develop and evaluate a clinician-guided software tool for measuring pediatric HC from routinely acquired 3D MRI examinations. Methods We developed a desktop application in Python using PySide6, the Insight Segmentation and Registration Toolkit, and the Visualization Toolkit for MRI-based HC measurement. The workflow included outer skin surface reconstruction, placement of 3 landmarks to define a freely orientable measurement plane, contour extraction, and circumference calculation. Optional Delaunay-based interpolation was implemented to reduce the influence of local cranial surface irregularities. In this retrospective evaluation, the tool was applied to 23 pediatric MRI examinations, including 18 without and 5 with clinically identified cranial surface irregularities. Two clinicians independently performed 3 repeated software measurements per examination. Median software measurements were compared with a single tape-based HC measurement obtained on the date of MRI. Agreement was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis, mean absolute error (MAE), proportional bias analysis, and a linear mixed-effects model. Interrater differences and preliminary usability feedback were also evaluated. Results Software-based HC measurement was feasible in all 23 examinations. In cases without cranial surface irregularities, the raw and interpolated contours showed similar agreement with tape-based measurements (bias 0.415 cm and 0.410 cm; MAE 0.429 cm and 0.423 cm, respectively). In the 5 examinations with irregularities, the intersection contour showed a greater bias of 1.420 cm and wider limits of agreement (LoA; -0.182 to 3.021 cm), whereas the interpolated contour showed a lower bias of 0.448 cm and narrower LoA (-0.119 to 1.014 cm). The estimated coefficient for the contour-by-subgroup interaction was -0.967 cm (SE 0.195 cm, 95% CI -1.349 to -0.584 cm; P <.001). No statistically significant proportional trend was detected, although the analysis had limited power to exclude proportional bias. Interrater differences were small. The 2 clinicians reported System Usability Scale scores of 92.5 and 95.0, representing preliminary descriptive feedback. Conclusions The clinician-guided workflow enabled MRI-based HC measurement in all examined cases and showed small interrater differences. Delaunay-based interpolation was associated with closer agreement with tape-based measurements in the small subgroup with cranial surface irregularities, while both contour variants performed similarly in examinations without irregularities. These findings are preliminary because of the small cohort, the single tape-based reference measurement per patient, and the 5-case irregularity subgroup. Larger studies using repeated reference measurements and broader cranial morphologies are needed to validate the workflow.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy and Fine-Grained Image-Interpretation Performance of Multimodal Large Language Models on Bilingual Radiology Questions: Cross-Sectional Benchmark Study.
abstract: Background Multimodal large language models (LLMs) are rapidly expanding in radiology and digital health; however, their diagnostic performance across diverse clinical scenarios and fine-grained visual reasoning tasks requires systematic evaluation. Objective The study aims to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy and fine-grained visual reasoning performance of 5 multimodal LLMs with bilingual medical imaging questions. Methods This cross-sectional benchmark study evaluated bilingual medical imaging questions using zero-shot prompting on 5 LLMs: GPT-5.2, Gemini 3 Pro, Doubao, Yuanbao, and Llama 4 Maverick. Subgroup analyses by language (English/Chinese), question type (image/text), imaging modality (computed tomography, radiography, magnetic resonance imaging, ultrasound, and nuclear medicine), and anatomical system (neurologic, respiratory, cardiovascular, digestive, genitourinary, and musculoskeletal) evaluated intermodel accuracy and intramodel consistency. Image-based visual reasoning performance was assessed across modality, anatomy, lesion detection, and localization. Results A total of 298 questions (198 image-based, 100 text-based) were evaluated. Gemini 3 Pro achieved the highest overall accuracy (n=268, 89.9%, 95% CI 86.0%-92.9%), significantly outperforming Doubao (n=235, 78.9%; P <.001), GPT-5.2 (n=233, 78.2%; P <.001), Yuanbao (n=216, 72.5%; P <.001), and Llama 4 Maverick (n=216, 72.5%; P <.001). All models performed better on text-based than image-based questions (Yuanbao, P <.001; Doubao, P =.02; GPT-5.2, P <.001; Gemini 3 Pro, P =.002; Llama 4 Maverick, P <.001). GPT-5.2 ( P <.001), Llama 4 Maverick ( P =.03), and Yuanbao ( P =.03) favored English questions, while intramodel performance remained stable across modalities (Yuanbao, P =.46; Doubao, P =.21; GPT-5.2, P =.26; Gemini 3 Pro, P =.96; Llama 4 Maverick, P =.45) and anatomical systems (Yuanbao, P =.82; Doubao, P =.52; GPT-5.2, P =.35; Gemini 3 Pro, P =.13; Llama 4 Maverick, P =.97). Despite near-perfect macroscopic visual recognition (modality and anatomy: 99.0%-100.0%), accuracy dropped in complex tasks. Gemini 3 Pro outperformed Yuanbao ( P <.001), GPT-5.2 ( P =.002), and Llama 4 Maverick ( P <.001) in lesion detection (175/198, 88.4%) and outperformed Yuanbao ( P <.001), Doubao ( P =.004), and Llama 4 Maverick ( P =.004) in lesion localization (189/198, 95.5%). Conclusions Gemini 3 Pro demonstrated optimal, comprehensive performance and cross-lingual stability. However, current multimodal LLMs face a technical bottleneck in complex visual interpretation-particularly in fine-grained lesion detection and localization-emphasizing the need to prioritize local feature perception in future model development.

title: Expert Perspectives on Transparency and Trust in AI-Based Clinical Decision Support Systems for Chest X-Ray Diagnosis: Qualitative Study.
abstract: Background The integration of AI-based Clinical Decision Support Systems (AI-CDSS) into clinical practice has expanded rapidly, particularly in medical imaging. Beyond algorithmic performance, growing evidence suggests that clinicians' engagement with AI-CDSS is shaped by how transparently systems communicate their outputs, and how trust is formed through human-AI interaction. However, a limited understanding of how these concepts are perceived by end users and developers continues to hinder real-world implementation. Objective This study aims to explore expert perspectives on transparency and trust in AI-CDSS for chest X-ray diagnosis, with a focus on the two-dimensional lens: user interface and users' mental models. Methods A qualitative study was conducted using semistructured interviews with a total of 21 experts, including 11 radiologists and 10 AI experts experienced in AI-CDSS. Data were analyzed thematically to explore factors perceived to influence transparent communication and trust. Results Three themes emerged: (1) perspective of transparency and trust, (2) user interface, and (3) users' mental models. Findings reveal that trust is a dynamic calibration process developed through repeated use, feedback loops, and alignment with clinicians' mental models, rather than algorithmic accuracy alone. Significant discrepancies were identified between how developers design system transparency and how clinicians interpret AI outputs. Conclusions This study demonstrates that transparency and trust are achieved through interpretable outputs, clear communication of system limitations, and alignment with clinical workflows. Designing trustworthy AI-CDSS requires integrating transparent interface design with consideration of users' knowledge, experience, and attitudes to support effective human-AI interaction.

title: Non-Invasive Monitoring of Bone Changes After Kidney Transplantation: Longitudinal Associations Between Microarchitecture, Density, and Early Biomarker Shifts.
abstract: Background Bone deterioration remains a frequent complication after kidney transplantation despite restored kidney function. Whether early post-transplant changes in circulating bone-related biomarkers are associated with subsequent site- and compartment-specific skeletal deterioration remains uncertain. Objectives To characterize first-year skeletal changes and determine whether biomarker changes from transplantation to 3 months are associated with 1-year skeletal deterioration. Methods Seventy-five kidney transplant recipients were prospectively followed from kidney transplantation to one year, with serial assessments of circulating bone-related biomarkers and skeletal imaging. Areal bone mineral density (aBMD) and bone microarchitecture were evaluated using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) and high-resolution peripheral quantitative computed tomography (HR-pQCT). title: Patient-Specific Virtual Reality for Lumbar Decompression Surgery: An Automated Imaging Pipeline and Educational Assessment
abstract: Manual construction of patient-specific models has limited the use of virtual reality (VR) for case-specific spine surgical rehearsal, and simulator assessments are often not patient-specific. We present a largely automated pipeline that converts routine preoperative CT and MRI into patient-specific 3D models for VR rehearsal of lumbar decompression, paired with case-specific written assessments. CT was segmented with an unmodified vertebral network and MRI with an in-house nnU-Net; volumes were registered and exported for VR. A locally hosted large language model generated per-case assessments from each patient's radiology report; the pipeline ran in approximately two minutes per case, and MRI segmentation reached a mean Dice of 0.870. Eight patient-specific models were prepared, and eleven trainees (undergraduate to fellow) completed a faculty-guided session with pre/post knowledge testing. Knowledge scores increased from 5.82 to 7.27 out of 10 (Wilcoxon $p=0.008$; Cohen's $d=1.01$), with 8 of 11 improving and none declining, and trainees rated educational value favorably. This feasibility study demonstrates a fast, fully private pipeline producing patient-specific VR models and matched assessments; the educational findings are preliminary and uncontrolled, motivating a larger controlled trial.

title: Feasibility of Augmented Reality-Guided Robotic Ultrasound with Cone-Beam CT Integration for Spine Procedures
abstract: Needle placement in spine interventions is critical for effective pain management, yet it depends on reliable identification of anatomical landmarks and careful trajectory planning. Conventional imaging guidance often relies on both computed tomography (CT) and X-ray fluoroscopy, exposing patients and staff to high doses of radiation while providing limited real-time 3D feedback. The choice of visualization may also affect operator performance and cognitive workload. We present an optical see-through augmented reality (OST-AR)–guided robotic system for spine procedures that provides in situ visualization of spinal structures to support needle trajectory planning. We integrate a cone-beam CT (CBCT)-derived 3D spine model, which is co-registered with live ultrasound, enabling users to combine global anatomical context with local, real-time imaging. We evaluated the system in a phantom user study involving two representative spine procedures: facet joint injection and lumbar puncture. Sixteen participants performed insertions under two visualization conditions: conventional screen vs. AR. Results show that AR significantly reduces execution time and across-task placement error, while also improving usability, trust, and spatial understanding, and lowering cognitive workload. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of AR-guided robotic ultrasound for spine interventions, highlighting its potential to enhance accuracy, efficiency, and user experience in image-guided procedures.

title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of SAM3 for Left Atrium Segmentation from MR Images for Improved Planning and Guidance of Cardiac Ablation Interventions
abstract: Foundation models such as Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM3) have demonstrated strong generalization in natural images through prompt-driven segmentation. However, their applicability to medical imaging remains unclear due to the domain-specific visual characteristics and task requirements. In this work, we investigate the domain adaptability of SAM3 for left atrium (LA) segmentation from cardiac MRI, a challenging, yet clinically critical task in the context of image-guided cardiac interventions, specifically aimed at improving planning and guidance of catheter-based cardiac ablation therapy in arrhythmia patients. We first evaluate SAM3 in a zero-shot setting using text prompts and show that performance remains limited despite descriptive prompt formulations, highlighting a fundamental mismatch between semantic prompting and the visual cues required for medical image segmentation. To address this limitation, we study two parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) strategies, including LoRA and a prompt-free adapter-based framework. Our comprehensive experimental results demonstrate that LoRA achieves stronger performance (Dice 90.6% and 91.7%) over zero-shot baselines and cross-dataset generalization. LoRA leverages the semantic priors, while the adapter provides stable predictions with improved computational efficiency. In particular, adapter training reduces per-epoch training time by over 7× compared to LoRA, while maintaining comparable segmentation performance. These findings reveal a key trade-off between generalization and efficiency and show that semantic guidance from text prompts and feature-level adaptation to modality-specific visual cues offer two viable, complementary pathways for adapting SAM3 to cardiac MRI. Our code is available here.
